stories.title: 📜 Philemon
summaryBullets: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our dear friend and fellow worker— (1:1).
also to Apphia our sister and Archippus our fellow soldier—and to the church that meets in your home: (1:2).
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. (1:3).
I always thank my God as I remember you in my prayers, (1:4).
because I hear about your love for all his holy people and your faith in the Lord Jesus. (1:5).
I pray that your partnership with us in the faith may be effective in deepening your understanding of every good thing we share for the sake of Christ. (1:6).
Your love has given me great joy and encouragement, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the Lord’s people. (1:7).
Therefore, although in Christ I could be bold and order you to do what you ought to do, (1:8).
yet I prefer to appeal to you on the basis of love. It is as none other than Paul—an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus— (1:9).
that I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, who became my son while I was in chains. (1:10).
Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me. (1:11).
I am sending him—who is my very heart—back to you. (1:12).
I would have liked to keep him with me so that he could take your place in helping me while I am in chains for the gospel. (1:13).
But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that any favor you do would not seem forced but would be voluntary. (1:14).
Perhaps the reason he was separated from you for a little while was that you might have him back forever— (1:15).
no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a dear brother. He is very dear to me but even dearer to you, both as a fellow man and as a brother in the Lord. (1:16).
So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me. (1:17).
If he has done you any wrong or owes you anything, charge it to me. (1:18).
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand. I will pay it back—not to mention that you owe me your very self. (1:19).
I do wish, brother, that I may have some benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ. (1:20).
Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask. (1:21).
And one thing more: Prepare a guest room for me, because I hope to be restored to you in answer to your prayers. (1:22).
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. (1:23).
And so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my fellow workers. (1:24).
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. (1:25).
crossRefs: Ephesians 1:15–16 — Thanksgiving for faith and love.
2 Corinthians 7:13 — Comfort and joy through others’ love.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָסִיר לַמָּשִׁיחַ (ʾāsîr la-māšîaḥ, sense) — Greek: δέσμιος Χριστοῦ (désmios Christoû, NT) — Aramaic: אסירא דמשיחא (ʾasirā d-mešiḥā)
translationNotes.note: Paul describes himself as imprisoned on account of his service to Christ.

stories.keyTakeaway: Paul greets Philemon and gives thanks for his love, faith, and the refreshment he has brought to the saints.
